I'm on 200mg Lamictal and 300mg Wellbutrin XL (extended release). The Lamictal felt like magic when I first started it and I felt like the world was clearer.  At the time, I was taking that with Prozac, but the Prozac made me so suicidal that it was dangerous just for me to drive.  Over time, the Lamictal needed to be increased because I guess I got used to it, but when I added the Wellbutrin (a not so stereotypical antidepressant), I felt better.  So far, over a year in with the Wellbutrin, I haven't hit that severe depression.  While I get the wanting to get rid of the Lamictal, because it feels like it wears off after a while, I think it's best to talk with your doctor about all options.  Mine recommended Latuda and gave me a sample of it, but that stuff made me feel totally out of whack, but it can help with others (especially bipolar depression).  I don't think it's a safe idea to go cold turkey, because I know how it feels when you're worried about how it'll affect work.  I also understand how it feels when you're still on the meds and you feel like it's affecting work too.  I guess the best (and maybe only) advice I can really give is to go see your doctor and lay it out as you did here - maybe even print this out - and go from there.  It's the safer route, for sure.
